title: Ideal Gas Equation

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 11 — States of Matter

explanation: The ideal gas equation combines Boyle's law, Charles's law, and Avogadro's law into a single relationship connecting pressure, volume, moles, and temperature for an IDEAL gas — one where molecules have negligible volume and no intermolecular forces. Real gases approximate this behavior well at low pressure and high temperature, but deviate significantly at high pressure or low temperature, where intermolecular forces and molecular volume become significant.

variables.meaning: Universal gas constant (0.0821 L·atm/mol·K, or 8.314 J/mol·K)

resultUnit: Depends on which variable is being solved for
conditions: T must always be in Kelvin, never Celsius
Assumes ideal gas behavior — best approximation at low pressure and high temperature

workedExample.scenario: 2 moles of an ideal gas occupy 10 L at 300 K.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to convert Celsius to Kelvin before substituting into the equation — a very frequent and entirely avoidable error.
Mixing R's value (0.0821 L·atm/mol·K) with pressure/volume units that don't match (e.g. using Pa and m³ with the atm-based R constant).
genZNote: PV=nRT will absolutely betray you if you forget the Kelvin conversion — Celsius is not invited to this formula.
